title: How to Edit Viral TikTok Clips in 2026

transcript.text: Alright so the first thing you need to understand about editing viral clips is that the hook is everything. You have exactly one point five seconds to grab attention.
The best hooks are either a shocking statement, a question that makes people curious, or a visual that's immediately attention grabbing.
For the zoom technique, you want to start with a slow zoom on the face during the hook. Like this. See how it draws you in?
Then when you hit the punchline or the emotional moment, you do a dramatic zoom. Quick, intense, like you're emphasizing the point.
The cut density is crucial. On TikTok, you want cuts every one to two seconds. Jump cuts work best. Remove every pause, every um, every uh.
Text overlays should be big, bold, and centered. Use white text with a black outline or red text for emphasis. The text should appear word by word to keep people reading.
For the energy curve, start at one hundred percent with the hook, drop to about sixty during the setup, then peak again at the punchline.
Sound effects are subtle but important. A whoosh at the hook, a boom at the punchline. Don't overdo it though.
The outro should be quick. Two seconds max. Fade to black or loop back to the beginning. Never say subscribe or follow, just end it.
Color grading for viral clips should be vibrant but not oversaturated. Slightly warm tones work best for face-focused content.
The total duration should be between fifteen and forty five seconds. Anything longer and you lose retention.
For captions, use word by word animation at the bottom. White text, clean font, good contrast against the background.

key_techniques: Slow zoom on face during hook
